mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes during a clear tightening cycle.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5.5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which pressures firms to raise wages and prices, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes under tight labor market conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) for three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes with confirmed consumer demand weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and suppresses earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of triggered episodes with confirmed industrial production contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A co-movement between rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) and falling payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 0.2 percentage points in the same month signals accelerating labor market deterioration, which depresses consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls by >0.2pp in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes where both UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls by >0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% for two consecutive months signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which increases real interest rates and erodes real earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both >2% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes under this dual shock.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a recovery in residential construction demand, which boosts materials and homebuilding sector earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes with confirmed housing starts recovery.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month in the same period signals a broad-based collapse in household demand, which reduces aggregate economic activity and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both fall >1% MoM in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of triggered episodes with confirmed broad household demand collapse.
